findings.title: Add/remove members read group_id but the route only sets id
findings.body: add_members and remove_member both do Group.find(params.require(:group_id)). The routes added in config/routes.rb are member routes (DELETE/PUT /admin/groups/:id/members), so Rails supplies params[:id], not params[:group_id]. The client also only puts the group id in the path (/admin/groups/:id/members.json) and does not send a group_id field. ParameterMissing (or a failed lookup) means adding and removing members from the admin UI will 400. Controller specs pass only because they inject group_id directly and never exercise the route.

findings.title: Member row template looks up fields on the wrong context
findings.body: group.hbs renders members with the non-block helper {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}. In this Ember version the item view's context is the user, and the named `member` binding is not available inside the item template. The template still uses {{member.username}}, {{avatar member}}, and {{action "removeMember" member}}, so avatars/usernames will not render and remove will be invoked without a user. `automatic` is also read from that user context, so the guard that hides the remove control for automatic groups does not work.

findings.title: Creating a group drops alias_level
findings.body: create only assigns name and visible from params. The client asJSON() also sends alias_level, and the new-group form exposes the alias-level combo box before the group has an id. That value is ignored, so every new group is stored with the default alias level (nobody) regardless of what the admin selected. Update does honor alias_level, so the setting only sticks on a later save.

findings.title: totalPages is one too high when count divides evenly
findings.body: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (the default page size is 50, so 50, 100, … members), this reports an extra empty page. showingLast then stays false on the real last page, so Next is enabled and loads a blank page. Use ceil(user_count / limit), and keep the zero-count special case.

findings.title: Members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit and offset
findings.body: limit and offset are taken straight from query params with no upper bound, no positive-only check, and no cap. Previously automatic groups were limited (default 200). Anyone who can see the group can now request an arbitrarily large page (or a negative offset, which PostgreSQL rejects). That can turn the public members list into a full dump and a cheap DoS. Clamp limit to a small maximum and reject negative offset/limit.

findings.title: Removing a member bypasses Group#remove
findings.body: remove_member deletes the user with group.users.delete(user_id), then calls group.save. The previous membership path used Group#remove, which is what add still uses (group.add). Association#delete skips Group#remove callbacks and any counter-cache, primary-group, or notification side effects that remove performs, so user_count and related state can stay stale after a successful admin removal.
